subject: Executive champion alignment & EB calendar lock
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Executive champion alignment & EB calendar lock

Hi Laura / Acme team —

Following up from last week's demo: as we discussed, getting an Executive Briefing (EB) window locked and confirming the champion(s) on your side will let us finalize the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and compress your evaluation timeline.

Quick proposal:
- EB window options (all PT): Nov 16 AM, Nov 19 PM, or Nov 23 AM. Each slot is 60–90 minutes.
- Desired attendees: your CIO (exec champion), procurement, and the product lead.
- Redwood will bring: VP Sales for strategic alignment, CS lead for deployment plan, and a technical engineer for architecture Q&A.

Attached: MAP draft (MAP_ACME_v1.2.xlsx), evaluation checklist. I also attached a provisional calendar (.ics) with the three windows.

Can you confirm: 1) who will be the executive champion, and 2) which EB window you prefer?

If we can lock an EB in the next week, we can accelerate the evaluation and hit the desired Nov 30 close target.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: MAP_ACME_v1.2.xlsx (spreadsheet), EB_slots_proposal.ics (calendar), Evaluation-Checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Executive champion alignment & EB calendar lock

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the clear options and materials. Quick answers:
- Executive champion: Our VP of Engineering, Rajiv Menon, will own this. Im looping in procurement and Samir (product).
- Preferred EB window: Nov 19 PM looks best for Rajiv and the leadership team.

Before we lock, two asks: can you tighten the evaluation checklist so we can hand it to our SRE and security reviewers? Also, does the MAP include proposed acceptance criteria for the pilot?

If you can send an updated MAP with acceptance criteria by EOD Wednesday, well confirm and send the calendar invite.

Best,
Laura Chen
Director, Product Strategy | Acme Corp
laura.chen@acme.com

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Executive champion alignment & EB calendar lock

Sean / team —

Thanks Laura. Ill take point on tightening the evaluation checklist and adding explicit acceptance criteria for the pilot (SRE, performance, security gates). Proposed additions:
- SRE gates: 99th percentile latency under 300ms for 8k token prompts during a 1-hour soak at expected QPS.
- Security gates: SOC2 evidence references + network flow overview for VPC/private deployment.
- Pilot acceptance: confirmed inference cost-per-1k tokens estimate within 15% of baseline, and a success rate >95% for prompt intent matching on our eval set.

Jordan, can you circulate the updated EB attendee list and confirm which Redwood exec will join? I recommend we include our Chief Product Officer for the strategic portion.

I will update the MAP spreadsheet and send a v1.3 by Wednesday EOD.

Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference

Great — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Laura: attached is MAP_ACME_v1.2 with an added "Acceptance criteria" tab; Evelyn will follow with the tightened SRE/security language. Highlights here:
- Milestone 1 (Pilot kickoff): Nov 9 — SRE onboarding & infra prep.
- Milestone 2 (Pilot evaluation): Nov 10–20 — daily evals + weekly checkpoint.
- Milestone 3 (EB & exec align): Nov 19 — formal exec briefing to validate ROI and sign-off readiness.
- Milestone 4 (Close target): Nov 30 — finalize PO & enablement.

Proposed EB agenda (60–90 min):
1) 10 min — Executive outcomes & business case (VP Sales + CPO)
2) 20–30 min — Technical deep dive & SRE Q&A (Engineer + Infra lead)
3) 15 min — Pilot acceptance criteria review (CS + Product)
4) 10–15 min — Next steps & procurement timeline (AE + Procurement)

If Nov 19 PM works, I will lock the provisional calendar and send the invite. If Rajiv needs a longer slot, we can expand to 90 minutes.

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_ACME_v1.2.xlsx (includes Acceptance criteria tab)

Sean / team —

Nov 19 PM is confirmed for Rajiv and the leadership team. Well need the tightened checklist (SRE/security specifics) to route to our security reviewers before the EB; can you send that by EOD Thursday?

Also, were trying to compress the evaluation by one week if possible. Is there scope to run a parallel smoke test while SRE finishes infra prep? If Redwood can commit an engineer to a 3-day focused pairing with our SREs starting Nov 9, we can likely shorten the pilot window.

Thanks — Ill have procurement circulate a draft PO following the EB.

Laura
